text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Serbian teachers protest outside republican government for eighth day over late and low wages. Most schools in Serbia still on strike. Serbian Education Minister Jovo Todorovic says government will do everything in its power to ensure lessons resume Wednesday.
- Economic policy at a crossroads -- either there will be a series of bankruptcies or printing of money will begin, threatening return to hyperinflation, says Belgrade Economics Institute.

- Radio Television Serbia has begun opening up, more opposition dailies and periodicals in Serbia than in most countries, Serbian Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic tells news conference in Washington.
- Zajedno (Together) coalition leaders Zoran Djindjic, Vuk Draskovic and Vesna Pesic leave on visits to Madrid and London.
- Textile workers of Serbia to begin strikes unless federal and republican governments take measures to ensure revival of production and wages.
- Belgrade university deans and students protest for 95th day demanding rector's resignation. University lectures in other major Serbian towns resume.

- Trziste Novca brokerage head Nikola Arandjelovic says latest central bank change in the reserve requirement to include both deposits and interbank credits has provoked new wave of mistrust. "Financial markets, banking sector and economy cannot expect better days."
- Health and social insurance workers to stage one hour warning strike demanding pay rise.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and Serb member of Bosnia-Herzegovina presidency Momcilo Krajisnik discuss advancing ties and common interests.
- Serbian government and metal workers trade union agree production growth is only way to improve social position of workers in metal complex.
- Yugoslav economy minister says energy consumption irrational, last year 8.8 percent above that in 1995. Around 3.8 million tonnes of crude oil to be imported this year.

- Zajedno coalition's appeal to citizens in municipalities where they won a majority not to pay electricity bills, taxes and communal services equal to calls to anarchy, Serbian television says in commentary.
- Federal Statistics Office introduces new method of calculating average wages. According to new method, pensions will be substantially reduced as well.
- Confederation of Montenegrin trade unions calls for removal of all political barriers for Montenegro's and Yugoslavia's return to international financial institutions.
